title: Historic vs dogmatic: Romans misread Reformed historic faith
source_text: XLVI. Non probant quoque, ut supra notatum est, Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores quod Reformati fidem illam historicam appellant, & dogmaticam potius dici malunt. Sed ut patet ex dictis, falluntur eorum plerique, dum putant Reformatos per historicam fidem intelligere solum illum assensum qui historiis Scripturae adhibetur, & quo historiae illae verae esse creduntur fide tantum humana, qualis etiam profanis historicis adhiberi solet. Etenim, ut jam dictum, Reformati fidei historicae nomine designant illam etiam quae divina quidem est, & toti Dei Verbo assensum praebet, sed otiosa tamen est & mere speculativa, quae communiter nomen fidei mortuae obtinet.
pass_a_gloss: The Doctors of the Roman Church also do not approve, as was noted above, that the Reformed call that faith historic and prefer it rather to be called dogmatic. But as is clear from what was said, most of them are mistaken when they think the Reformed by historic faith mean only that assent which is given to the histories of Scripture, and by which those histories are believed to be true with merely human faith, such as is also customarily given to profane historians. For, as already said, by the name of historic faith the Reformed designate even that which is indeed divine and gives assent to the whole Word of God, yet is idle and merely speculative, which commonly obtains the name of dead faith.
pass_b_english: Rome dislikes the Reformed historic label and prefers dogmatic, but most Romans misread historic as mere human assent to Scripture stories.
Reformed historic faith names divine assent to the whole Word that remains idle and speculative — commonly called dead faith.

lemmas.gloss: yet is idle and merely speculative

choices.why: Divine idle assent, not human history-belief.
rejected: historic = only believing Bible stories humanly
